headline: Pixxel closes $100M, Skyroot reaches orbit, and a fusion start-up makes plasma
dek: Almost every profile on the radar now shows the evidence behind its scores, and new TRL estimates are based on real tests.

sections.title: Money moved
sections.note: Closed rounds only. Reported talks never count.

items.name: Pixxel
items.meta: Co-led by Temasek and Seraphim · 7 Sep 2026
items.body: Builds hyperspectral satellites. A normal camera sees red, green and blue. Pixxel's cameras see hundreds of colour bands, enough to tell a healthy crop from a stressed one, or spot a gas leak from space. Earlier reports had this round only "in talks". It's now confirmed closed.

items.name: Quanfluence
items.meta: Led by Chiratae Ventures, with pi Ventures and Rainmatter · Oct 2026
items.body: Its machine uses light instead of electrons to find the best answer among huge numbers of options, like routing trucks or scheduling a factory. It's the strongest team on the radar this week, with evidence for all 4 team factors. Three founders are ex-Texas Instruments chip designers who built Silabtech and sold it to Synopsys. Two are physics professors at IIT Madras and IISER Mohali. It also holds a granted Indian patent.

items.name: TakeMe2Space
items.body: Puts computers on satellites so images can be processed in orbit before they're sent down. This replaces the 2025 pre-seed as its last confirmed round.

items.text: pi Ventures led Velmenni's ₹30 Cr pre-Series A (Li-Fi, which sends data through light). GIC and Sherpalo Ventures co-led Skyroot's Series C.

sections.title: Things that actually worked
sections.note: Each TRL now rests on a dated, public milestone.

items.name: Skyroot · Vikram-1 reached orbit
items.body: Reached orbit on its first orbital launch, from Sriharikota.

items.name: Pranos Fusion · first plasma
items.body: Built PRAGYA, a small tokamak: a doughnut-shaped chamber that uses magnets to hold extremely hot gas. It then reported producing plasma inside it. That's step one on a very long road to fusion power.

items.name: SatLeo · thermal camera in space
items.body: Its TAPAS-1 payload launched aboard Dhruva Space's LEAP-2 satellite. No images from orbit yet, so the radar puts it one level below the company's own claim until results come in.

items.name: Aule Space · docking test at ISRO
items.body: Tested its guidance and docking system in ISRO's Rendezvous Simulation Lab. Aule wants to dock with ageing satellites and keep them working for longer.

items.name: OrbitAID · demo lost on PSLV-C62
items.body: Its in-orbit refuelling demo was on PSLV-C62, which failed and didn't reach orbit. Its profile now notes this.
